adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (in server-spi-private) has a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` added. This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of this interface. The `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` method iterates over all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. This is a real binary compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — [P2/C75] `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut();` makes decoding issued tokens depend on the currently installed factory's mutable shortcut, so changing or removing a grant provider during a deployment makes every still-valid token carrying its previous shortcut undecodable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), grant shortcuts are populated from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() at startup. If a grant provider is later removed or its shortcut changes, tokens encoded with the old shortcut cannot be decoded because getGrantTypeByShortcut() will fail to find the mapping. The code does attempt to refresh maps dynamically, but if a provider is removed entirely, previously issued tokens with that shortcut become undecodable. This is a correctness issue for token lifecycle management.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 — [P2/C100] `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut` instructs extension authors to return a value that `encodedContext.length() != 6` rejects after encoding, so a custom grant following this API contract produces token IDs that always fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException`.

The Javadoc says '3-letters shortcut' but looking at the actual implementations in the diff (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', 'pg', 'te', 'ro', 'pc'), all shortcuts are 2 characters, not 3. The encodedContext is 6 characters total: 2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType. The Javadoc comment is slightly misleading ('3-letters' vs actual 2-char shortcuts), but this is just an imprecise documentation comment, not a functional bug. The actual code works correctly with 2-character shortcuts, and all built-in implementations use 2 characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — [P2/C75] `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` installs a lazily discovered grant without the startup collision check, so deploying a grant with an existing shortcut silently remaps previously issued token IDs to the new grant type instead of rejecting the conflicting provider.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue. In postInit(), there's a collision check that throws IllegalStateException if grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(), which would catch duplicate shortcuts at startup. However, in getGrantTypeByShortcut() (lines 108-123) and getShortcutByGrantType() (lines 95-106), when a grant is lazily discovered after startup, it's added directly to the maps without any collision check. If a newly deployed grant has a shortcut that already exists, it would silently overwrite the existing mapping (grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)), causing previously issued tokens with that shortcut to be decoded as the new grant type instead of the original one. This is a correctness/security bug.
